uncited: This family generalizes isosurface extraction from 3D spatial grids to $n$-dimensional domains (typically 4D, representing 3D space plus time or another parameter) by treating the isosurface as a hyper-surface within the higher-dimensional volume.

It solves the problem of extracting topologically correct surfaces from high-dimensional scalar fields where standard 3D algorithms like [Marching Cubes](30-isosurface-extraction.md) fail due to combinatorial explosion or topological ambiguity.

It sets itself apart from sibling methods by operating directly on $n$-dimensional hypercubes or simplices to define the surface geometry, rather than projecting 3D slices or using learning-based approximations.
